mappings.note: Which Government of India Act first allowed elected representation; the colonial origin of India's representative institutions, which no LO covers -> goal-level.
Who demanded elected members in the legislature; the pre-independence demand for representation -> goal-level.
Participation as the take-off point for democracy; a principle of the democratic system -> goal-level.
How a citizen gives consent to the government (by voting) -> LO-13, the election process, rather than the institutional goal.
Which house is made of representatives elected by the people; naming the institution -> goal-level, with LO-13 kept for the process itself.
MLAs represent the state legislature; the State level as distinct from the Union -> LO-12.
Year the Lok Sabha was constituted -> goal-level.
Leading party in the 2014 general election; an outcome of the Lok Sabha election -> LO-13.
Members nominated to the Rajya Sabha by the President; the composition of a house -> goal-level, since LO-13 is specifically about Lok Sabha elections.
Interval between Lok Sabha elections -> LO-13 directly.
Which party is based in Maharashtra; parties are the contestants in the election process -> LO-13. No outcome covers party systems on their own.
Leader of the ruling party in the Lok Sabha (the Prime Minister); an office of the Union executive -> goal-level.
The house that represents the states is the Rajya Sabha; the federal State/Union distinction -> LO-12.
Members nominated to the Lok Sabha; the house's composition rather than its election -> goal-level.
Who heads the Rajya Sabha -> goal-level, an institutional office.
Parliament as the law-making body -> goal-level.
Seats needed for a majority in the Lok Sabha; how the election produces a government -> LO-13.
Elected strength of the Rajya Sabha; composition of the upper house, outside LO-13's Lok Sabha scope -> goal-level.
Elected strength of the Lok Sabha, i.e. one member per constituency -> LO-13.
What Zero Hour is; parliamentary procedure -> goal-level, no LO covers it.
Who is responsible for the country's sanitary conditions. Sanitation is a public facility, which CG-SST6 names as a state responsibility; no LO in curriculum 131 covers public facilities.
The combined parties short of a majority are the Opposition; a parliamentary role -> goal-level.
Types of Bills; the legislative process -> goal-level.
How Parliament controls the executive; accountability between organs -> goal-level.

For whom parliamentary seats are reserved (Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes) -> LO-16, which names those groups; not LO-13, since the item is about representation of marginalised groups rather than the polling process.
Who chooses the representatives to Parliament -> LO-13.
The word for a situation with no easy solution (dilemma); chapter vocabulary -> goal-level.
What Parliament lets citizens take part in; the function of the institution -> goal-level.
Chairman of the Rajya Sabha -> goal-level, an institutional office.
Naming Parliament as the highest law-making body of the two houses -> goal-level.
What PMO stands for; an office of the Union executive -> goal-level.
Which house is the upper house -> goal-level.
Which house is the lower house -> goal-level.
Who exposes the weaknesses of policy (the Opposition) -> goal-level.
To whom the President submits a resignation -> goal-level, an institutional procedure.
One member elected per constituency -> LO-13. LO-14 names constituencies but requires locating one's own and naming its MP, which this item does not ask.
Presidential election disputes are settled by the Supreme Court. LO-17 is about judges delivering justice to litigants, so the competency describing the judiciary's role is the right level.
Parliament's chief function -> goal-level.
What Parliament consists of -> goal-level.
The Rajya Sabha's other name (Council of States) -> goal-level; LO-12 is reserved for items that turn on the State/Union division rather than on a name.
